SHOP OF HORRORS - Five gunned down outside Seawinds winkel in brazen daylight attack

Marsha Dean|Published 19 hours ago

BLOODSHED: Police tape cordons off the scene in Seawinds

Image: Supplied

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:47
Instaread

RESIDENTS in Seawinds have described the scene as “gruesome” after five people were shot outside a corner tuckshop on Tuesday afternoon, leaving two men dead and three others wounded.

Multiple shots rang out on the corner of Mossie and Penguin streets at about 4pm when occupants of a white vehicle opened fire people outside the shop.

Western Cape police spokesperson Sergeant Wesley Twigg confirmed Muizenberg police registered two counts of murder and three of attempted murder following the shooting in Mossie Street.

“Two males in their thirties were declared deceased on the scene by medical personnel, while the other victims [including a 53-year-old woman] were transported to a medical facility for treatment,” Twigg said.

“According to reports, occupants of a vehicle drove up to the victims and opened fire on them before fleeing the scene. The motive for the attack is believed to be gang-related.”

A nearby community activist recalled: “I went to fetch my printouts, and while I was in the building, they started shooting so much that we all had to duck and dive, and everybody who was in the road had to flee.

“It was a drive-by shooting; the suspects got out of the vehicle with massive guns and started shooting. The victims were unsuspecting because they were standing at the shop which is on the corner. There were also children standing at the shop.

“There were so many bullets on the scene after the shooting. I believe AK-47s were used. People were shot, and the scene was gruesome. I had to leave because I could not take it.

“It is not going to stop until they get what they want, but they were warned. You can’t afford to walk around in your own neighbourhood because you are not safe.”

Although police have not named specific gangs, an unverified warning circulated on community groups and sent to community leaders days earlier urged parents to keep their children away from the area, claiming gunmen threatened to return “by force”.

Another resident said: “My son just left that corner after fetching his two children from the school transport when they started shooting. These jongens don’t care; they shoot at the police as well.”

Twigg added that Anti-Gang Unit detectives are investigating, while Operation Prosper deployments remain in the area to restore calm.

Meanwhile, a planned Thursday protest in Lavender Hill was called off after SAPS advised against it due to operational constraints.

The attack follows Monday night’s shooting in Military Road, Lavender Hill, where a nine-year-old girl was wounded around 8.30pm. Steenberg police are investigating attempted murder after she was taken to a medical facility privately in a stable condition.

Anyone with information on the Seawinds shooting can contact Crime Stop on 08600 10111 or via the MySAPS app.

How this consent management platform (CMP) works:

CMP privacy choices

Storage, duration, and usage details

The choices you make with this CMP regarding the purposes and entities will affect how personalized advertising is presented to you. We need to store these choices to respect them on future visits, and they are stored differently based on the type of site or app you're using:
  • For sites, your choices are saved in a cookie named “FCCDCF” for a maximum duration of 390 days.
  • For apps, your choices are saved in device storage prefixed by “IABTCF_”. Your choices will be invalidated after 390 days and overwritten once you make new privacy choices on this app.
  • For accelerated mobile page (AMP) sites, your choices are saved in local storage prefixed by “amp-store”. Your choices will be invalidated after 390 days and overwritten once you make new privacy choices on this site.
